title: Decisions for the Icelandic word-bluff game

entities.title: Approve Phase 1 and start building the game
entities.summary: Phase 1 found 391 verified, usable words (280 of them at obscurity 2–3), above the 200 needed. The research recommends GO; the owner decides.
entities.context: The owner asked for the game in two phases and for Phase 2 not to start until Phase 1 is approved. Phase 1 had to show at least 200 verified words that are real, obscure, not given away by their parts, short to define and suitable.

options.title: GO
options.consequences: Phase 2 builds the game: lobby with room code, rounds, voting, scoring, reveal with source link, big-screen view, reconnects, custom words.

options.title: Revise the list first
options.consequences: The owner or another native speaker reviews the sample and the uncertain wording; words are dropped or reworded before the build.

entities.origin: The owner's request for the game, in a Claude Code session, 23 November 2026

entities.title: How to handle rare senses of common words
entities.summary: A large share of the words are a rare sense of a word everyone knows (rjúpa = hnykill, áróður = róður móti straumi). Decide whether the game hints at this or lets the host filter them out.
entities.context: These make good bluffs, but a player who writes the common meaning may feel cheated when it is not counted as correct.

options.title: Show a hint such as "sjaldgæf merking" with the word
Let the host leave such words out
Do nothing; the host's "essentially correct" button covers disputes
